correctness.rationale: The proof reduces each antithetic pair to one signed standard Cauchy variable and uses independence plus the Cauchy characteristic function to obtain the exact scale \(A=\sum_j|w_{j,+}-w_{j,-}|\). The reported p-value is a monotone transform, yielding the full cdf directly from the scaled-Cauchy tail. The exactness criterion, strict-conservatism regime, Gaussian realization, and small-\(\alpha\) limit all follow analytically. Numerical checks are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The dependence model is natural: independent Gaussian contrasts can generate two opposite one-sided p-values, and recent heavy-tailed-combination work identifies negative-correlation conservatism as a methodological issue. The theorem gives a complete finite-level classification for any number of independent antithetic pairs through the cancellation budget \(A\), showing precisely when standard Cauchy calibration remains exact, becomes conservative, or collapses entirely. This is a structural boundary result rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
